answer_md:
No, that idea is not supported by the evidence. The Great Pyramid was built by a large, organized human workforce, and the records back that up in detail.

Construction gangs marked their blocks with painted graffiti naming their crew and the pharaoh, a normal job-tracking practice[^1]. The Heit el-Ghurab settlement near the Sphinx housed that workforce with bakeries, worker and elite housing, and administrative buildings, the footprint of a real logistics operation[^2]. The Diary of Merer, a papyrus found in 2013, logs limestone deliveries from Tura to Giza dated to year 27 of Khufu's reign, an ordinary supervisor's shipping record[^3]. Separate papyri from Wadi al-Jarf, also from that same year, show the central administration sending food and supplies to sailors and wharf workers[^4].

As for how the stones moved, only small ramps and inclined causeways survive in the archaeological record[^5], and a paved causeway cut into bedrock still exists at Giza[^6]. A calculation using an assumed block mass, an assumed 8 degree ramp, an assumed friction coefficient of 0.3, and an assumed pull of 400 N per person shows a crew of about 27 people can haul such a block, well within ordinary human capability and needing no unexplained technology.

The evidence points to skilled organization and administration, not aliens.

citations.title: The Pyramids and Temples of Gizeh (Petrie, 1883)

rows.ancient: The strip leveled around the pyramid base perimeter was measured to be horizontal and flat to within 21 millimetres.
rows.evidence: "only a strip around the perimeter was leveled, which has been measured to be horizontal and flat to within 21 millimetres (0.8 in)" (Great Pyramid of Giza (Wikipedia), section: Rediscovery)
rows.modern: Laser level survey confirming site grading tolerance before foundation pour.
rows.lesson: Precise leveling of only the load-bearing perimeter, not the whole footprint, can achieve tight tolerances efficiently.

rows.ancient: The Diary of Merer, a papyrus discovered in 2013, records deliveries of limestone from Tura to Giza in year 27 of Khufu's reign.
rows.evidence: "In 2013, rolls of papyrus called the Diary of Merer were discovered, written by a supervisor of the deliveries of limestone from Tura to Giza in the 27th year of Khufu's reign." (Great Pyramid of Giza (Wikipedia), section: Materials)
rows.modern: A logistics manager's daily delivery log tracking material shipments to site.
rows.lesson: Keep detailed, dated delivery records to verify supply chain performance and enable later audits.

rows.ancient: The archaeological record shows only small ramps and inclined causeways, not ramps that could have built even most of the monument.
rows.evidence: "The archaeological record gives evidence of only small ramps and inclined causeways, not something that could have been used to construct even a majority of the monument." (Construction of the Egyptian pyramids (Wikipedia), section: Transport of stone blocks)
rows.modern: Using temporary access ramps or haul roads to move material up a rising structure.
rows.lesson: Physical remains of temporary construction aids should be preserved and documented as they reveal actual build sequencing.

rows.ancient: Construction gangs building the Great Pyramid marked stone blocks with painted graffiti naming their gang and incorporating the pharaoh's name.
rows.evidence: "The workers who were building the pyramid had marked the blocks with the names of their gangs, which included the pharaoh's name" (Great Pyramid of Giza (Wikipedia), section: Purpose)
rows.modern: Marking precast or delivered structural elements with the crew or subcontractor identifier and job code.
rows.lesson: Tag materials with crew and project identifiers so provenance and accountability can be traced later.

rows.ancient: Many casing stones and inner chamber blocks of the Great Pyramid fit together with joints averaging only 0.5 millimetres wide.
rows.evidence: "Many of the casing-stones and inner chamber blocks of the Great Pyramid fit together with high precision, with joints, on average, only 0.5 millimetres (0.020 in) wide." (Great Pyramid of Giza (Wikipedia), section: Workforce)
rows.modern: Fine masonry joint tolerances comparable to precision dimension-stone cladding work.
rows.lesson: Put the tightest tolerances on the faces and joints that matter most, like casing and chamber linings.
